correctness.rationale: Rotating a distinguished sampled point to zero makes the remaining circular spacings uniform on the (n-1)-simplex. Translating distinct exceedance coordinates and rescaling the remaining simplex gives the positive-part power in (5), including zero mass at saturation. In the mixed second moment the same-gap term uses s by nesting, while the distinct-gap term uses r+s; subtracting the product of means gives (1). Dividing by the positive factor n(1-s)^(n-1) yields the strictly decreasing bracket before s=1-r and its constant plateau thereafter. The plateau yields r_c, which is at most 1/2 since n<=2^(n-1), with equality only at n=2. Below r_c the variance at s=r is strictly positive: open simplex sets give exactly one and at least two exceedances. This supplies the unique interior crossing, and solving the bracket gives the stated s_*. At r=r_c the zero plateau includes all admissible s for n=2. For the PGF, each factor is 1+(u-1)I_r+u(v-1)I_s, so disjoint coordinate selections yield the claimed exact multinomial sum. Expanding the exact powers at r=x/n,s=y/n gives the stated kernel, and its positive diagonal and strict sign crossing justify bracketing the finite root; e^x-1>x^2 for x>0 follows from e^x>=ex>2x for the derivative comparison. Independent rational polygon clipping of the n=3 simplex at r=1/10 and s=3/5 gives means 243/100 and 12/25 and product moment 51/50, hence covariance -183/1250.
